headline: Microsoft 365 outage takes down Outlook, Teams and Copilot worldwide
summary: A widespread Microsoft 365 outage knocked out Outlook, Teams and Copilot for roughly a day, affecting governments, hospitals, schools and businesses worldwide, with some Japanese workers resorting to fax machines. Microsoft gave shifting explanations for the cause, and outlets disagree on whether a cyberattack was ruled out and on exactly how long the disruption lasted.

claims.statement: A major outage hit Microsoft 365 services including Outlook, Teams and Copilot.

sources.quote: Multiple Microsoft 365 services are experiencing an outage
Massive Microsoft 365 outage disrupts Outlook, Teams, Copilot worldwide

claims.statement: Microsoft initially attributed the outage to elevated load across multiple regions.

sources.quote: We've determined a portion of infrastructure is experiencing elevated load across multiple regions

claims.statement: The Register reported Microsoft had not completely ruled out a cyberattack as the cause.

sources.quote: Hasn't completely ruled out cyberattack as cause of incident

claims.statement: Microsoft later said the outage was not caused by a cyber-security incident.

sources.quote: the outage was not caused by a cyber-security incident

claims.statement: Microsoft ultimately said a bad update, not a cyberattack or AI, crashed its servers worldwide.

sources.quote: a bad update—not a cyberattack or AI—caused its servers around the world to crash

claims.statement: Microsoft also said the outage was due to a technical failure, for which it apologized.

sources.quote: Microsoft has apologised for the issue, which it said was due to a technical failure.

claims.statement: Governments, hospitals, courts, schools and businesses worldwide were affected.

sources.quote: Governments, hospitals, courts scrambled by global Microsoft outage.
The House of Representatives, health care providers, schools and many other organizations were affected.
businesses, schools, hospitals, and governments have found out the hard way

claims.statement: Some Japanese workers resorted to fax machines to cope with the outage.

sources.quote: Japanese workers are breaking out fax machines to deal with Microsoft's 365 outage.

claims.statement: An expert said the outage may be worse than past Amazon or CrowdStrike incidents.

sources.quote: Microsoft’s global outage may be worse than Amazon's or CrowdStrike's, expert says

claims.statement: Service gradually began recovering, with some users regaining email access while other features stayed degraded.

sources.quote: Service is gradually starting to recover for Microsoft Outlook and 365

discrepancies.explanation: The Register reported Microsoft had not ruled out a cyberattack as the outage's cause, while the BBC later reported Microsoft said the incident was not a cyber-security incident.

quotes.quote: Hasn't completely ruled out cyberattack as cause of incident
the outage was not caused by a cyber-security incident

discrepancies.explanation: The BBC attributed the outage's cause to servers unexpectedly becoming unavailable, while Wired reported Microsoft blamed a bad update.

quotes.quote: the outage was caused by servers unexpected becoming unavailable, straining other systems
a bad update—not a cyberattack or AI—caused its servers around the world to crash

discrepancies.explanation: The Verge described the outage as lasting almost two days, while Wired put its length at 24 hours.
